title: Discussion + hook: give cloned plugins an update path (auto-sync forks on omarchy update)
head: 7dd996df701a
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Flat bar widget sources have only sibling manifests, so the hook never reapplies identity or updates their manifest
leads.consequence: For stock clones of active-window, indicators, keyboard-layout, microphone, spacer, system-update, tray or workspaces, catalog.sourceDir is the shared shell/plugins/bar/widgets directory, which has *.manifest.json but no root manifest.json. build_new therefore never calls apply_identity. First baseline contains all sibling files, but no clone manifest; on later runs diff adds the fork's old manifest.json as a 'local edit' to every new upstream tree, so upstream changes to the source widget's manifest never reach the fork. The patch also deletes the other sibling widgets' files and can conflict on unrelated changes to them; new sibling files may enter the fork. Select the catalog.manifestPath and copy that manifest as fork/manifest.json, with the entry point and clonePaths exactly as omarchy-plugin-clone does.

leads.summary: No validity check precedes replacing an installed fork
leads.consequence: When upstream changes manifest entryPoints, kinds or schemaVersion, or the user's patch edits its manifest incompatibly, patch can return success even though resulting plugin is invalid. The hook removes the working fork and calls rescanPlugins; PluginRegistry rejects invalid manifests or fails to load missing entry points. The add and update commands validate before using/updating plugins, but this hook never calls omarchy-plugin-validate on staged new content. Validate the merged directory before swapping and notify without mutating the fork if invalid.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator from source (hook never calls omarchy-plugin-validate; add/update do); published as optional note labelled 'From source, not run', wording corrected after self-check flag 7

leads.summary: Fork removal does not retire its baseline, so a later fork reusing its ID inherits another fork's history
leads.consequence: After omarchy-plugin-remove moves a clone to a hidden backup, its $STATE/<id>/baseline remains. Re-cloning the same source under the same derived ID, or replacing it by hand with a different clonedFrom, skips first-encounter protection and diffs against the former clone's snapshot. A new fork can be rewritten on its first update or stuck on conflict. Track the origin and fork instance as well as ID, retire state on remove, or require explicit re-baselining when identity changes.

leads.summary: A failing copy or write can be followed by deleting the live fork and still claim it was updated
leads.consequence: set -uo pipefail omits errexit. cp/build_new/diff errors are not gated; after patching, cp into $fork_dir.sync.$$ can fail (full disk, inaccessible file) but rm -rf $fork_dir still runs and mv publishes an incomplete directory. Similarly an error copying a new baseline after rm -rf $base_dir leaves state permanently incomplete and the hook exits 0. Treat all steps as transactions, test each return, and swap with rollback rather than remove-before-move.

leads.summary: Catalog errors are interpreted as 'all upstreams disappeared'
leads.consequence: If omarchy-plugin-catalog fails (for example a malformed manifest causes its jq to exit nonzero), catalog is replaced by []. The loop sends a misleading critical 'upstream missing' notification for every tracked fork and exits success. Check the catalog status/shape once and report the catalog failure without labeling upstreams removed or mutating state.
leads.triage: factual, verified from source by coordinator; Opus then ran it (review-5 bad-manifest); published as optional note

leads.summary: New opt-in sample never arrives in an existing user's hooks directory on normal update
leads.consequence: The settings PKGBUILD copies config/** into /etc/skel and /usr/share/omarchy/config, but /etc/skel seeds only newly created users; normal omarchy update and migration do not resync configs into existing homes. Existing users following the PR's 'remove .sample suffix' instruction will not find this file at ~/.config/omarchy/hooks/post-update.d until they manually copy it from /usr/share/omarchy/config/..., or run the destructive reinstall configs command. Document the package path and safe explicit installation/rename for upgrades.

leads.summary: Catalog labels a user's reserved-namespace manifest as firstParty despite shell rejecting it
leads.consequence: omarchy-plugin-catalog sets firstParty solely by id.startsWith('omarchy.'), even for user-directory manifests which PluginRegistry explicitly rejects as impersonating a built-in. If a fork's clonedFrom points to such an otherwise absent ID, this hook treats its user directory as upstream and copies arbitrary user plugin files to its baseline and fork (the intended source is not a bundled plugin). Require a sourceDir/manifestPath underneath the trusted first-party root and validate the catalog entry, not just firstParty and id. The case requires a manually crafted manifest, not ordinary omarchy plugin clone.
leads.triage: dropped: requires a hand-crafted reserved-namespace manifest, not reachable through omarchy plugin clone; low value

leads.summary: Hook's core state transitions have no matching repository test
leads.consequence: The hook has no test fixture exercising baseline initialization, conflict, idempotence, swap, catalog errors, or clonePaths. plugin-clone-test.sh tests cloning/removal, plugins-test.sh checks first-party manifests, and hook-state-name-guard-test.sh checks hook names, none invokes this hook. A plausible mutant replacing 'build_new' with a whole directory copy would pass them while breaking sibling widgets and rebaselining. Add a test/shell.d/*-test.sh with a stub catalog, fork and two successive upstream revisions and assertions on contents/state and fail-safe conflicts.
leads.triage: already in Opus optional notes (no tests); not published separately

flags.claim: any change there leaves an unedited clone conflicting on each update
flags.why: Not any change. A change limited to the cloned widget's own QML syncs cleanly, and a new file added to bar/widgets/ syncs too (and is copied into the fork). A conflict follows from a change to another widget's existing files (s1, quattro b18ab495 Tray.qml/ActiveWindow.qml) or to the widget's own *.manifest.json.

flags.claim: A fork is first seen after an update, so earlier upstream changes replay as reversed edits
flags.why: Lost qualifier. The hook is usually first run by omarchy update, but the header says it is safe to run by hand any time (hook line 23); a run right after cloning records the correct baseline. My report said 'normally'. 'earlier upstream changes' should be the changes made since the clone.

flags.claim: Removing and re-cloning a plugin (which the manual suggests after a mess)
flags.why: The manual suggests removing ('if you make a mess of it, omarchy plugin remove dhh.clock puts the built-in back'); it does not suggest cloning again. My reproducer description says '(the documented way to start over)', which has the same problem.

flags.claim: The only way out is deleting ~/.local/state/omarchy/plugin-forks/<id>, which nothing mentions.
flags.why: Absolute. From code, undoing the local change (case: identical upstream change) makes the patch empty and the next run syncs; deleting the state dir is the general way out (review-1 s5). The path also follows XDG_STATE_HOME (hook line 29). 'nothing mentions' holds for the recovery step; the header names the state directory (line 24) but not deleting it. Low priority; my report has the same absolute.

flags.claim: In a synthetic plugin with two similar blocks, an edit to the second block landed in the first
flags.why: Lost trigger condition: this happened after upstream changed the lines around the edit (renamed id, recoloured, visible false). Without that, patch applies exactly and fuzz is not used.

flags.claim: no copy, rm or mv is checked
flags.why: Line 127 is 'rm -rf "$fork_dir" && mv "$newperm" "$fork_dir"', so the mv runs only if the rm succeeded, and line 66 gates a mv on jq. What holds: no cp is checked, and a failed rm or mv does not stop the baseline advance (line 128) or the success notification (line 130). My report's '(no status checks)' for lines 126-128 has the same overstatement.

flags.claim: omarchy-plugin-add and -update run omarchy-plugin-validate on staged content
flags.why: Only -add validates staged content (bin/omarchy-plugin-add:125, stage .add.tmp.$$). omarchy-plugin-update validates the live checkout after 'git merge --ff-only' and rolls back with 'git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD' on failure (bin/omarchy-plugin-update:67-76). The second half is correct: the hook never calls omarchy-plugin-validate.

flags.claim: The hook deletes and renames a plugin directory under the shell's plugin watcher, the situation reported in issue #12859.
flags.why: #12859 (an issue, not a PR; confirmed with gh api) reports omarchy plugin update rewriting a plugin checkout's files under the watcher (git merge --ff-only), not a directory delete and rename. It is a similar situation, not the same one.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** In common cases the hook leaves clones stuck in conflict or silently reverts upstream fixes.

### Bar-widget clones stay in conflict

Eight bar widgets share `bar/widgets/` as `sourceDir`, so baselines hold all 18 files there, not the clone's 2. A change to another widget's files or the widget's manifest keeps an unedited clone in conflict on every update, and Indicators' `indicators/` never syncs, without notice.

**Suggested change:** Copy upstream as `omarchy-plugin-clone` does.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 7dd996d)</summary>

# Reproducer: Flat bar widget clones: false conflicts and unsynced clonePaths

Two tests. The first clones `omarchy.workspaces`, records the baseline, then changes `Tray.qml` in the shared `bar/widgets/` directory (the edit quattro shipped in b18ab495). The unedited Workspaces clone is reported as a conflict. The second clones `omarchy.indicators` and changes `bar/indicators/Dnd.qml` upstream; the clone never receives it and no notification is sent.

Add the file(s) below to `test/shell.d/` in a checkout of the PR head (7dd996df) and run them with `bash test/shell.d/<file>`. They use the repository's `base-test.sh`, the real `omarchy-plugin-clone`, `omarchy-plugin-catalog` and `omarchy-plugin-remove` from `bin/`, and stub `omarchy-shell`, `omarchy-notification-send` and `omarchy-plugin-enable`. Everything is written under a `mktemp -d` directory. Needs `jq`, `patch`, `rg` (and `git` for the git case).

## `test/shell.d/sync-plugin-forks-flat-widget-test.sh`

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

require_command jq
require_command patch
require_command rg

HOOK="$ROOT/config/omarchy/hooks/post-update.d/sync-plugin-forks.hook.sample"
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
export TMPDIR
trap 'chmod -R u+w "$TMPDIR" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$TMPDIR"' EXIT
home="$TMPDIR/home"
plugins="$home/.config/omarchy/plugins"
state="$home/.local/state/omarchy/plugin-forks"
upstream="$TMPDIR/omarchy/shell/plugins"
CALLS="$TMPDIR/calls"
mkdir -p "$plugins" "$TMPDIR/bin" "$TMPDIR/omarchy/shell"
cp -a "$ROOT/shell/plugins" "$upstream"

cat >"$TMPDIR/bin/omarchy-shell" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'omarchy-shell %s\n' "$*" >>"$FAKE_CALLS"
if [[ $* == *listPlugins* ]]; then
  find "$HOME/.config/omarchy/plugins" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name manifest.json -print0 |
    xargs -0 -r jq -s 'map({id: .id, enabled: true})'
fi
exit 0
SH
for command in omarchy-notification-send omarchy-plugin-enable; do
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nprintf "%%s %%s\\n" "${0##*/}" "$*" >>"$FAKE_CALLS"\n' >"$TMPDIR/bin/$command"
done
chmod +x "$TMPDIR/bin/"*

in_env() {
  HOME="$home" XDG_STATE_HOME="$home/.local/state" USER=tester OMARCHY_PATH="$TMPDIR/omarchy" \
    PATH="$TMPDIR/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" FAKE_CALLS="$CALLS" "$@"
}

clone_plugin() {
  in_env omarchy-plugin-clone "$1" >/dev/null
}

# Run the enabled sample the way omarchy-hook runs post-update.d entries.
sync_forks() {
  : >"$CALLS"
  in_env bash "$HOOK"
}

# An unedited clone of a flat bar widget (widgets/*.manifest.json).
clone_plugin omarchy.workspaces
sync_forks # first run records the baseline

# Upstream changes a different widget that shares the widgets/ directory
# (the same edit quattro shipped to Tray.qml).
sed -i 's/duration: root.animationDuration;/duration: Style.duration(root.animationDuration);/' "$upstream/bar/widgets/Tray.qml"
sync_forks

if grep -q 'needs attention' "$CALLS"; then
  fail "an unedited Workspaces clone syncs after an unrelated Tray.qml change" \
    "$(cat "$CALLS")
baseline: $(ls "$state/tester.workspaces/baseline" | tr '\n' ' ')
fork:     $(ls "$plugins/tester.workspaces" | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi
pass "an unedited Workspaces clone syncs after an unrelated Tray.qml change"
```

### First run takes the wrong baseline

A fork is usually first seen right after an update, when upstream may already differ from the cloned version. Those changes then replay as reversed edits: an unedited weather clone lost quattro's `reduceMotion` fix.

**Suggested change:** Record the baseline in `omarchy-plugin-clone`, and do not merge forks whose base is unknown.

<details><summary>More findings: Clean syncs lose fork content</summary>

Rebuilding the fork as upstream plus a text diff drops what a text diff cannot carry: user-added binary and empty files are deleted, scripts lose the exec bit, a fork kept under git loses its objects, and a symlinked fork becomes a copy. The notification still says "your edits kept".

**Suggested change:** Write only the files upstream changed, merged per file, and skip git and symlinked forks.

**Reproducer (fails at 7dd996d)**

# Reproducer: A clean sync drops content a text diff cannot carry

After a successful sync that reports "your edits kept": a user-added binary file and empty file are deleted, a new script loses its executable bit, a fork kept under git loses its objects and index, and a fork that is a symlink to the user's checkout is replaced by a copied directory.

<details><summary>More findings: Conflicts never clear</summary>

The baseline advances only on success and is keyed by plugin id. <details><summary>More findings: patch defaults are not fail-safe</summary>

GNU patch applies hunks with fuzz 2 by default. In a synthetic plugin with two similar blocks, an edit to the second block, after upstream changed the lines around it, landed in the first ("succeeded at 2 with fuzz 2 (offset -6 lines)") and the hook reported "your edits kept". With a plain offset on the real weather panel, patch wrote `Panel.qml.orig`, which was copied into the live fork. The approach is a two-way diff replay rather than the 3-way merge the header describes.

**Suggested change:** Merge per file with `git merge-file -p <fork> <baseline> <new>` and treat a non-zero exit as a conflict, or at minimum pass `--fuzz=0 --no-backup-if-mismatch`.

<details><summary>More findings: Partial failures replace the fork and still report success</summary>

The script runs with `set -uo pipefail` and no `-e`; no copy is checked, and a failed `rm` or `mv` does not stop the baseline advance or the success notification. <details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (sandbox runs at 7dd996d):
- First encounter records a baseline and leaves the fork alone; for all 30 first-party plugins with a plain `manifest.json`, the baseline equals a fresh clone byte for byte.

- A real conflict leaves the fork byte-identical and sends the notification.
- User file deletions replay correctly.

**Optional notes:**
- Every notification uses `-u critical`, which in the Omarchy shell never expires; "Now tracking plugin fork" and "Plugin fork updated" are informational, and "upstream missing" repeats on every update.
- In a sandbox run, a truncated user plugin manifest made `omarchy-plugin-catalog` fail (its single `jq` call covers every manifest); the hook fell back to `[]` and sent "upstream missing" for every fork.
- From source, not run: `omarchy-plugin-add` validates the staged checkout and `omarchy-plugin-update` validates after merging and rolls back on failure; this hook never validates what it swaps into the live fork.

Not tested: behaviour with a running shell. The hook deletes and renames a plugin directory under the shell's plugin watcher, similar to the crash reported in issue #12859.
